elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement will not exceed..." — "each Party" binds both PB and SFJ.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted cap reads only "the fees paid or payable under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim"; there is no greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 15.11: "NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL, RELIANCE OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES..."; mirrored by the mutual waiver in 15.10.2.4.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "Excluded Claims" expressly includes "breach of its confidentiality obligations", and Excluded Claims sit outside the new cap.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The Excluded Claims definition lists only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct; no data protection or security carve-out appears.
"'Excluded Claims' means a Party's indemnification obligations..." — Article 12 indemnities sit outside the cap.
Excluded Claims include "willful misconduct" (US spelling of wilful misconduct).
Fraud is absent from the Excluded Claims definition, so fraud claims are capped.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out in the Excluded Claims definition; IP infringement claims fall inside the new cap.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Retained final sentence of 15.11 ("THIS SECTION 15.11 IS NOT MEANT TO LIMIT PB'S OBLIGATION TO PAY SFJ THE AMOUNTS SET FORTH IN ARTICLE 6 OR SECTION 14.2") sits in the same Section as the new cap, but it is expressly limited to two enumerated payment sources rather than PB's payment obligations as a whole; whether Article 6 and Section 14.2 exhaust PB's payment obligations cannot be confirmed from the cited text.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement will not exceed..." — symmetrical as to both PB and SFJ.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: The cap is pegged to "the fees paid or payable under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim", but this Co-Development Agreement contains no "Fees" concept — its payment streams are Development Costs and the Article 6 / Section 14.2 payments — and the sentence does not say which Party's payments are counted. The 12-month magnitude is therefore indeterminate and risks an illusory (near-zero) cap on SFJ.
"'Excluded Claims' means a Party's indemnification obligations...", and the cap opens "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Excluded Claims include "breach of its confidentiality obligations".

reasons: Finding classification is correct: Section 15.11 and the arbitration waiver in 15.10.2.4 exclude consequential damages mutually but impose no aggregate monetary cap anywhere (including Article 12 indemnities), so the clause fails the fallback and a redline is warranted.

Fallback is not complete because the cap basis is indeterminate. The inserted sentence uses "the fees paid or payable under this Agreement", but this agreement defines no "Fees" and its consideration flows are Development Costs, Article 6 Approval/milestone payments and Section 14.2 termination amounts. Repair the operative language, e.g. "...will not exceed the aggregate amounts paid or payable by PB to SFJ under Article 6 and Section 14.2 in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim" (or another expressly identified payment stream), and state which Party's payments form the measure.

Directional silence compounds the defect: as drafted the measure could be read as either Party's payments, which leaves SFJ's exposure (the exposure we care about) capped by an amount we may not control.

Preferred level fails on four separate elements: no greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor, and no uncapped carve-out for data protection/security breaches, fraud, or infringement of the other Party's intellectual property. If the counterparty accepts more than the fallback, add those to the Excluded Claims definition and the greater-of floor to the cap sentence.

The preferred Customer-payment element is only partially served: the retained "for the avoidance of doubt" sentence preserves PB's obligations under Article 6 and Section 14.2 only, not PB's payment obligations generally; if any other PB payment obligation exists it would be swept inside the new cap.

Minimality is satisfied: the drafter added a single concise sentence pair to a section that lacked any cap, retained the favourable mutual consequential-damages exclusion and the PB-payment carve-out, and added no survival tail, expense language, procedures or carve-outs beyond the fallback checklist.

Intent is preserved: the arbitration damages waiver, Article 12 indemnities, Article 6 payment mechanics and the deemed-consequential-damages sentence all survive without contradiction; the new cap sits within Section 15.11 so the existing PB-payment carve-out continues to disapply it to PB's Article 6 / 14.2 payments.
